title: Road Trip Overnight Stop Planner
description: Split a long drive into days and name the overnight towns with the Road Trip Overnight Stop Planner — cap the miles, keep the trip human. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 1,350-mile drive capped at 450 miles a day becomes three days with two overnight towns named — the trip planned around sleep, not bravado.
quick_answer: The Road Trip Overnight Stop Planner routes your drive, caps how far you travel in a day — by miles or by days — and names the town near each overnight stop. Set start, destination and the daily limit, and read where each day ends and how far it runs.
steps_intro: Long drives are a chain of human days. Cut the chain at sleeping distance:

body.t: The relocation drive becomes stages with towns — bookable, shareable, survivable. The
counts the days; this planner places them.
Children and grandparents set the real daily cap. Plan the overnights at their distance and the trip stays a holiday.
One driver, no relief: the cap is a safety device. Stages named in advance remove the 'one more hour' negotiation at dusk.
Named overnight towns can be priced tonight. An unnamed 'somewhere around mile 700' cannot.
At a 450-mile cap: three days, two overnights, each named where the day's miles run out. The same drive at a 600 cap is two brutal days — the planner shows both, the human chooses.
Four days fixed for the same route reverses the question: the planner divides and names the stops, and the daily miles fall where the calendar puts them.

faq: Does it book hotels?
No — it names the overnight towns, which is the decision booking sites cannot make for you. Book the town it names.
Can I split by number of days instead?
Yes — fix the days and the planner divides the route across them, naming each night's town.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Stages are distance-shaped; a day of mountain roads deserves a lower cap than a day of interstate, and your judgement sets it.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Stages end at road miles. A town 400 crow-miles away can be 460 by road — the planner works in the honest unit.
Can route results change over time?
Roads change slowly; towns do not move. Re-run a standing route each year, mostly for the roadworks.
What daily cap is sensible?
For most drivers 400–500 miles on fast roads, less on slow ones. Your last trip's honest average — from the Road Trip Average Speed Calculator — calibrates it.
Can I add stops of my own?
Yes — waypoints join the route and the stages re-form around them. A must-see town bends the plan, correctly.
The named town has no rooms that night.
Take the next town along the route — the planner's spacing still holds; only the pillow moved. Book early in festival country.
Can stages be in two countries?
Happily — the route crosses borders without noticing, and the towns named are simply where the miles end.
I drive an EV — different stops?
Your daily cap may be set by charging rather than fatigue. The stages still frame the days; chargers choose among the towns.
